finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches a caller-supplied URL with axios. The only check is that the string starts with "https://", which restricts the scheme but not the host. An attacker can point the server at internal HTTPS hosts or at any attacker host that redirects. axios follows redirects by default, including https to http, so the redirect can land on http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/. The response body is not returned, only its byte length (`bytes`), so this is blind or semi-blind SSRF (internal probing, port and host scanning, response-size oracle). Severity MEDIUM per the skill's blind-SSRF rule. Redirect risk: yes.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl (JSON body of POST /profile/avatar, unauthenticated as far as the code shows)

trace.note: const url = req.body.avatarUrl; attacker-controlled JSON body field
Validation: typeof string and startsWith("https://"). This is a prefix and scheme check only, with no hostname allowlist and no private-IP or DNS-resolution check
axios.get(url) with default maxRedirects (follows redirects with no per-hop re-validation) fetches the attacker-chosen host
Only img.data.length is returned to the caller, so the body is not exfiltrated directly. The size is leaked and reachability can be inferred from success or failure

finding.guards_checked: Scheme prefix check (https:// only) is insufficient per the skill: it is a prefix check, not strict hostname set membership. There is no hostname allowlist, no IP or CIDR blocking, and redirects are not disabled (no maxRedirects: 0), so an https:// URL can redirect to http:// internal or metadata targets. No authentication middleware exists in server.js. No egress controls are present in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a scheme prefix check, url.startsWith("https://"), at server.js:11; no host allowlist, no IP blocking, no maxRedirects limit, no auth middleware)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl, server.js:11 only checks the "https://" prefix (not a closing guard), and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirect following, returning only the byte length at server.js:15, so this is blind SSRF.
